stack.name: Android Developer
stack.summary: A 12-week plan to pass senior Android interviews: Kotlin and coroutines in depth, Flow, platform internals and the Android 16/17 changes, Jetpack Compose internals and at scale, architecture and DI, offline-first data, builds and release, testing, performance and security, and mobile system design.

weeks.goal: Answer Kotlin questions at the level of semantics and generated bytecode, since Kotlin is in 94% of senior Android postings and interviewers test it first.
weeks.title: Kotlin in depth

lessons.title: The type system: nullability, generics and variance
topics: Nullable types, smart casts, platform types from Java and `!!`
Generics: declaration-site variance (`in`/`out`), use-site projections and star projection
`inline` functions, `reified` type parameters, `crossinline` and `noinline`
`Nothing`, `Unit` and `Any` in the type hierarchy
lessons.exercise: Write a `reified` inline helper that parses JSON into a type, and explain from the bytecode why it works only because it is inlined.

lessons.title: Classes that model state: sealed, value and data classes, delegation
topics: Sealed classes and interfaces for UI state and results; exhaustive `when`
Data classes: generated members, `copy`, and pitfalls with mutable properties
Value (inline) classes and when they are boxed
Delegation: `by lazy` (thread-safety modes), `Delegates.observable`, class delegation
lessons.exercise: Model a screen's loading, content and error states as a sealed interface and write an exhaustive renderer.

lessons.title: Lambdas, collections, sequences and the K2 compiler
topics: Scope functions (`let`, `run`, `with`, `apply`, `also`): when and why
Lambdas and allocation: captured variables, SAM conversions
Collections vs sequences: eager vs lazy evaluation and when sequences win
The K2 compiler: what changed for smart casts and build speed
lessons.exercise: Benchmark a filter-map-take chain on a list and on a sequence, and explain the difference in work done.

lessons.title: Idiomatic API design in Kotlin
topics: Extension functions and properties: resolution is static
Designing APIs with default and named arguments, and `@JvmOverloads` for Java callers
Type-safe builders and DSLs with lambdas with receivers
Java interop: `@JvmStatic`, `@JvmField`, nullability annotations and checked exceptions
lessons.exercise: Design a small type-safe builder DSL for a network request and review it for Java callers.

milestones.title: Refresh your CV and LinkedIn for senior Android roles: lead with scale, ownership and shipped apps
DSA track: 20-30 minutes a day on arrays and hash maps (big-tech loops are DSA-heavy)

weeks.deliverable: A small Kotlin library (a typed result wrapper and a few extension-based APIs) with notes on what each feature compiles to.
interview_checks: What does `inline` do to a lambda, and why is `reified` only allowed on inline functions?
Is `lazy` thread-safe by default? When would you choose `lateinit` instead?
Explain `in` and `out` variance with a real Android example.
When would you use a sealed interface over an enum class?

weeks.goal: Explain how coroutines suspend, switch threads, cancel and fail, since this is the single most-asked topic in senior Android interviews.
weeks.title: Coroutines internals

lessons.title: Suspension, continuations and dispatchers
topics: How `suspend` compiles: continuation-passing style and the state machine
Dispatchers: Main, Main.immediate, Default, IO and `limitedParallelism`
`withContext` and what a context switch costs
`CoroutineContext` elements: Job, dispatcher, name, exception handler
lessons.exercise: Decompile a two-step suspend function and point out its state machine labels.

lessons.title: Structured concurrency
topics: Scopes and the Job hierarchy: parents wait for children
`viewModelScope`, `lifecycleScope` and why `GlobalScope` is discouraged
`coroutineScope` vs `supervisorScope`, `Job` vs `SupervisorJob`
Injecting dispatchers and scopes for testability and work that must outlive a screen
lessons.exercise: Load a profile and its feed in parallel with `async`, and make one failure cancel or not cancel the other on purpose.

lessons.title: Cancellation and exception handling
topics: Cooperative cancellation: `isActive`, `ensureActive`, `yield` and cancellable suspend points
Not swallowing `CancellationException` (the most common production coroutine bug)
Exception propagation, `CoroutineExceptionHandler` and where it actually works
`NonCancellable` and cleanup in `finally`; `withTimeout` vs `withTimeoutOrNull`
lessons.exercise: Write a CPU-heavy parser that honors cancellation, and a `runCatching` wrapper that does not swallow cancellation.

lessons.title: Testing coroutines and interview traps
topics: `runTest`, virtual time and `advanceUntilIdle`
`StandardTestDispatcher` vs `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` and `Dispatchers.setMain`
Testing timeouts, retries and cancellation
Common traps: blocking calls in coroutines, `runBlocking` on the main thread, leaked scopes
lessons.exercise: Test a retry-with-backoff function using virtual time so the test runs in milliseconds.

milestones.title: DSA track: two pointers and sliding window, 20-30 minutes a day

weeks.deliverable: A repository class with parallel network calls, timeouts and cancellation, plus tests that prove cancellation and error handling work.
interview_checks: What is the difference between `launch` and `async`, and how do their exceptions differ?
What happens when a child coroutine fails inside `coroutineScope` versus `supervisorScope`?
Why is catching `CancellationException` a bug, and how do you avoid it?
Cancelling a search stops the request but parsing keeps running. How do you fix it?

weeks.goal: Use Flow correctly for UI state and data streams: hot vs cold, the right operators, lifecycle-safe collection and tests.
weeks.title: Flow and reactive state

lessons.title: Cold and hot streams
topics: Cold flows: each collector runs the producer
StateFlow: conflation, equality and the initial value
SharedFlow: replay, buffer and `onBufferOverflow`
`stateIn` and `shareIn` with `SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000)`
lessons.exercise: Turn a repository flow into UI state with `stateIn` and show what happens on rotation with each `SharingStarted` policy.

lessons.title: Operators and backpressure
topics: `flatMapLatest`, `flatMapConcat` and `flatMapMerge`
`combine` vs `zip`; `debounce`, `distinctUntilChanged`
`buffer`, `conflate` and `collectLatest` for slow collectors
`catch`, `retry`, `onCompletion` and exception transparency
lessons.exercise: Build a search pipeline: debounce input, cancel stale requests with `flatMapLatest`, and recover from errors without ending the flow.

lessons.title: Bridging callbacks and lifecycle-aware collection
topics: `callbackFlow` and `awaitClose` for listeners; `channelFlow`
`flowOn` and which context upstream code runs in
`repeatOnLifecycle`, `flowWithLifecycle` and `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`
One-off UI events: channels vs state, and the trade-offs
lessons.exercise: Wrap a location or connectivity callback API with `callbackFlow` and collect it safely from a screen.

lessons.title: Testing Flow and migrating from RxJava
topics: Testing flows with Turbine: `test`, `awaitItem`, `awaitComplete`
Testing StateFlow in a ViewModel
RxJava to Flow interop (`asFlow`, `asObservable`) for legacy code
Mapping Rx concepts to Flow: Subjects, Schedulers, Disposables
lessons.exercise: Write Turbine tests for last lesson's search pipeline, including the error path.

milestones.title: Apply to five senior Android roles (remote boards, LinkedIn and Bdjobs), each with a tailored summary
DSA track: stacks, queues and binary search, 20-30 minutes a day

weeks.deliverable: A search screen's state pipeline built with Flow (debounce, flatMapLatest, stateIn) and Turbine tests for it.
interview_checks: What is the difference between a cold Flow and a hot StateFlow or SharedFlow?
When would you use SharedFlow instead of StateFlow for events?
Why use `repeatOnLifecycle` or `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` to collect in the UI?
How do you wrap a callback-based API as a Flow?

weeks.goal: Explain what the OS does to your app (processes, the main thread, IPC and background limits) and ship code that meets the current targetSdk 36 requirements.
weeks.title: Platform internals, background work and the Android 16/17 changes

lessons.title: Processes, lifecycles and process death
topics: Process priority and how the OS picks what to kill
Activity and Fragment lifecycles, configuration changes
How ViewModel survives configuration change (ViewModelStore) but not process death
SavedStateHandle and `rememberSaveable`; testing process death
lessons.exercise: Kill your app's process from adb while it is in the background and fix every piece of state that does not come back.

lessons.title: The main thread, Looper and Binder
topics: Looper, Handler and MessageQueue, and Android 17's lock-free MessageQueue
What blocks the main thread and how that becomes an ANR
Binder and IPC: how app components talk to system services
Intents, tasks and the back stack
lessons.exercise: Trace a click from input event to your handler, and draw how the message reaches the main thread's queue.

lessons.title: Background work
topics: WorkManager: constraints, unique work, chaining, expedited work
Foreground service types and the permissions each requires
Doze, App Standby buckets and background execution limits
Choosing between coroutines, WorkManager and a foreground service
lessons.exercise: Build a periodic sync worker with network and battery constraints and a retry policy.

lessons.title: Android 16/17 and Play targetSdk 36
topics: Google Play's target API requirement and deadlines
Android 16: mandatory edge-to-edge, predictive back on by default, large-screen orientation and resizability changes
Android 17: behavior changes that break reflection, mandatory resizability, notification limits
Running a targetSdk migration safely: compatibility flags and testing
lessons.exercise: Bump a sample app to targetSdk 36, list every behavior change that affects it, and fix each one.

milestones.title: DSA track: linked lists and trees, 20-30 minutes a day

weeks.deliverable: A sync feature using WorkManager with constraints and a correctly typed foreground service, plus a targetSdk 36 migration checklist for your app.
interview_checks: What happens between tapping the launcher icon and the first frame?
How does a ViewModel survive a configuration change, and what survives process death?
How do Looper, Handler and MessageQueue work together?
WorkManager, a foreground service or a coroutine: how do you choose?

weeks.goal: Explain how Compose works under the hood (phases, snapshots, recomposition and stability) now that Google has made Android Compose-first.
weeks.title: Jetpack Compose internals

lessons.title: Phases and the snapshot system
topics: Composition, layout and draw phases, and which phase reads a state
Deferring state reads to later phases (lambda modifiers)
The snapshot system: how state writes schedule recomposition
Positional memoization and the slot table
lessons.exercise: Move a scroll-driven animation's state read from composition to the draw phase and measure the difference.

lessons.title: Recomposition, stability and Strong Skipping
topics: Stable, immutable and unstable types; `@Stable` and `@Immutable`
Strong Skipping mode and how lambdas are remembered
Compose compiler reports and metrics
Unstable collections and classes from other modules
lessons.exercise: Generate compiler reports for a screen, find the unstable parameters and fix them.

lessons.title: State and side effects
topics: State hoisting and unidirectional data flow in Compose
`remember`, `rememberSaveable` and state holders
`LaunchedEffect`, `DisposableEffect`, `rememberUpdatedState`, `SideEffect`
`derivedStateOf`, `snapshotFlow` and `produceState`
lessons.exercise: Fix a screen whose effect restarts on every recomposition, and one that captures a stale callback.

lessons.title: Compose performance lab
topics: Lazy lists: keys, content types and item reuse
Avoiding work in composition: `remember` for expensive calculations
Layout Inspector recomposition counts and system tracing
Baseline Profiles for Compose apps
lessons.exercise: Work through the Compose performance codelab and write up the three biggest wins.

milestones.title: Build: start a portfolio app (Compose, MVVM, Hilt, Room, offline) in the shape of a take-home test
DSA track: graphs (BFS/DFS), 20-30 minutes a day

weeks.deliverable: A Compose screen profiled with compiler reports and Layout Inspector, with unnecessary recompositions removed and a note on each fix.
interview_checks: What triggers recomposition, and how does Compose decide to skip a composable?
What makes a type stable, and what did Strong Skipping change?
What is the difference between `remember` and `rememberSaveable`?
When would you use `LaunchedEffect` versus `DisposableEffect`?

weeks.goal: Build Compose UIs a team can scale: a design system, Navigation 3, adaptive layouts, edge-to-edge, predictive back, accessibility and migrating from Views.
weeks.title: Compose at scale

lessons.title: Design systems and theming
topics: Material 3 theming: color schemes, typography, shapes, dynamic color
Building reusable components and slot APIs
CompositionLocal: when to use it and when not
Previews and a component catalog
lessons.exercise: Build a themed button and card with slot APIs and light, dark and dynamic-color previews.

lessons.title: Navigation 3 and adaptive layouts
topics: Navigation 3: a state-driven back stack that you own
Type-safe routes, deep links and passing arguments
Window size classes and canonical layouts (list-detail, supporting pane)
Large-screen and foldable requirements from Android 16/17
lessons.exercise: Add a list-detail layout that shows two panes on tablets and one pane on phones, sharing the same back stack.

lessons.title: Edge-to-edge, predictive back and accessibility
topics: Window insets: `safeDrawing`, IME insets and consuming insets
Predictive back: `BackHandler`, `PredictiveBackHandler` and animations
Semantics: content descriptions, merging, roles and touch target size
Testing with TalkBack and the accessibility scanner
lessons.exercise: Make a screen fully edge-to-edge with the keyboard handled, and fix every issue TalkBack finds.

lessons.title: Interop and migrating from Views
topics: `ComposeView` and `AndroidView`; interop with Fragments
Migration strategy: new screens first, shared components, then old screens
Views are in maintenance mode: what that means for planning
Measuring migration progress and performance regressions
lessons.exercise: Write a migration plan for a 40-screen Views app, with ordering, risks and how you would measure progress.

milestones.title: Apply to five more roles and ask two people in your network for referrals
DSA track: heaps and intervals, 20-30 minutes a day

weeks.deliverable: Your portfolio app with a small design system, Navigation 3, a list-detail layout on large screens, edge-to-edge and TalkBack support.
interview_checks: How would you structure a design system in Compose for several feature teams?
What changed with Navigation 3, and who owns the back stack?
How do you support large screens now that orientation locks are ignored at 600dp and wider?
How do you migrate a large Views app to Compose incrementally?

weeks.goal: Own an app's architecture: UDF and UI state, layer boundaries, MVVM vs MVI trade-offs, and DI scoping that does not leak.
weeks.title: Architecture and dependency injection

lessons.title: UI layer: UDF, state production, MVVM and MVI
topics: Unidirectional data flow: state down, events up
Producing UI state from multiple sources
MVVM vs MVI: reducers, intents and when each fits
ViewModel responsibilities and what never belongs in it
lessons.exercise: Rewrite a screen from several LiveData fields into a single immutable UI state produced by a StateFlow.

lessons.title: Layers and boundaries
topics: Data, domain and UI layers; the dependency direction
Repositories as the single source of truth
Use cases: when a domain layer helps and when it is overkill
Mapping models between layers
lessons.exercise: Decide, with reasons, which of your app's features need use cases and which do not.

lessons.title: Hilt and Dagger in depth
topics: Hilt components, their lifetimes and scope annotations
Leaks from scope mismatch (holding an Activity in a singleton)
Qualifiers, multibindings, assisted injection and entry points
Compile-time DI (Hilt/Dagger) vs runtime service location (Koin)
lessons.exercise: Create a scope-mismatch leak, catch it with LeakCanary, and fix it with the right component.

lessons.title: Architecture review
topics: Reading a large codebase: module graph, data flow and conventions
Now in Android's architecture decisions and their trade-offs
Writing an architecture decision record
Presenting an architecture review in an interview
lessons.exercise: Review Now in Android and present, in 10 minutes, three decisions you agree with and one you would change.

milestones.title: DSA track: dynamic programming basics, 20-30 minutes a day

weeks.deliverable: An architecture review of Now in Android plus your portfolio app refactored to the recommended layers, with Hilt scopes documented.
interview_checks: MVVM or MVI? What trade-offs make you choose one?
When is a domain layer overkill?
An injected singleton keeps an old Activity alive after rotation. Where is the scope mismatch?
Why use Hilt over manual DI or Koin in a large team?

weeks.goal: Build a data layer that works offline, syncs correctly and handles the network well, and know when Kotlin Multiplatform can share it.
weeks.title: Data layer, networking and offline-first

lessons.title: Networking
topics: OkHttp interceptors, authenticators and connection pooling
Retrofit with coroutines and a Result-style error model
Auth token refresh without duplicate calls
HTTP caching, timeouts and retries; REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC for mobile
lessons.exercise: Implement token refresh so that ten parallel requests with an expired token trigger only one refresh.

lessons.title: Local persistence: Room and DataStore
topics: Room: entities, DAOs, relations and Flow queries
Migrations, auto-migrations and testing them
Transactions and threading
DataStore (Preferences and Proto) vs SharedPreferences
lessons.exercise: Write and test a Room migration that splits one column into two without losing data.

lessons.title: Offline-first, sync and paging
topics: Local database as the single source of truth
Sync strategies: pull, push, change tokens and conflict resolution
Paging 3 with a RemoteMediator
Showing sync state and errors in the UI
lessons.exercise: Add a RemoteMediator-backed paged feed that keeps working in airplane mode.

lessons.title: Kotlin Multiplatform for the data layer
topics: KMP structure: common, Android and iOS source sets
`expect`/`actual` and platform-specific code
Sharing networking (Ktor) and persistence (Room KMP or SQLDelight)
When to adopt KMP and how to introduce it to an existing team
lessons.exercise: Move your app's data models and one repository into a shared KMP module.

milestones.title: Apply to five more roles and follow up on earlier applications
DSA track: mixed medium problems under a 30-minute timer

weeks.deliverable: Your portfolio app made offline-first: Room as the source of truth, a sync worker, Paging 3 and a network layer with auth refresh.
interview_checks: How do you design an offline-first app, and how do you resolve sync conflicts?
How would you refresh an expired auth token without firing duplicate requests?
DataStore or SharedPreferences: why was DataStore introduced?
When would you adopt Kotlin Multiplatform, and what would you share first?

weeks.goal: Scale the codebase and the build: module strategy, fast Gradle builds, R8, and a release pipeline to Google Play.
weeks.title: Modularization, builds and delivery

lessons.title: Modularization
topics: Feature, core and library modules; api vs implementation modules
Dependency rules and preventing cycles
Navigation between feature modules
Measuring the benefit: build times and team ownership
lessons.exercise: Split one feature out of your app into its own module with an api/impl boundary.

lessons.title: Gradle and build speed
topics: Kotlin DSL, version catalogs and convention plugins
Configuration cache, build cache and parallel execution
KSP vs kapt
Build variants, product flavors and build types
lessons.exercise: Replace duplicated module build scripts with a convention plugin and measure the build before and after.

lessons.title: R8, app size and app bundles
topics: R8: shrinking, obfuscation, optimization and keep rules
Debugging R8 problems: mapping files and missing classes
Android App Bundles and Play Feature Delivery
Measuring and reducing app size
lessons.exercise: Enable R8 full mode, fix whatever breaks, and compare download size before and after.

lessons.title: CI/CD and Play releases
topics: CI with GitHub Actions: build, test, lint on every pull request
Signing and Play App Signing; managing secrets in CI
Play tracks, staged rollouts and halting a rollout
In-app updates and forcing an update
lessons.exercise: Build a pipeline that uploads a signed bundle to the internal testing track with fastlane.

milestones.title: DSA track: two timed mock coding rounds

weeks.deliverable: Your app split into feature and core modules with convention plugins, R8 enabled, and a CI pipeline that ships to an internal test track.
interview_checks: How would you modularize a large app, and what rules keep modules independent?
How do you speed up a slow Gradle build?
What does R8 do, and what breaks when you enable it?
How do you roll out a risky release on Google Play?

weeks.goal: Design a test strategy for a whole app, since testing is in 65% of senior postings and weighs heavily in take-home reviews.
weeks.title: Testing strategy

lessons.title: Test strategy and test doubles
topics: The test pyramid for Android: local, instrumented and end to end
Fakes, stubs and mocks; when MockK helps and when it hurts
Designing code for testability (injected dispatchers, interfaces at boundaries)
What reviewers look for in a take-home's tests
lessons.exercise: Replace a mock-heavy repository test with a fake and compare how each breaks when the code changes.

lessons.title: Testing ViewModels and repositories
topics: Testing state produced with StateFlow
Using `runTest` and test dispatchers with ViewModels
Testing flows with Turbine
Testing Room with an in-memory database
lessons.exercise: Write tests covering loading, success, error and retry for a ViewModel.

lessons.title: Compose UI and screenshot tests
topics: Compose testing: semantics, finders and assertions
Synchronization and idling in Compose tests
Robolectric for fast UI tests on the JVM
Screenshot testing for design systems
lessons.exercise: Write a Compose UI test for your list-detail flow and a screenshot test for one component.

lessons.title: Tests in CI
topics: Running unit and instrumented tests in CI (managed devices, emulators)
Causes of flaky tests and how to fix them
Coverage: useful signal or vanity metric
Walking through a take-home rubric
lessons.exercise: Make your CI run all test types on each pull request and fail fast on the cheapest checks.

milestones.title: Practice: complete a timed take-home (fetch, list, detail, offline, tests) in one day

weeks.deliverable: Your portfolio app with unit, ViewModel, Compose UI and screenshot tests running in CI, and a short testing strategy document.
interview_checks: How do you decide what to unit test and what to UI test?
Fakes or mocks: which do you prefer, and why?
How do you test a ViewModel that uses coroutines and Flow?
How do you deal with flaky UI tests?

weeks.goal: Diagnose and fix real performance problems (startup, jank, memory, ANRs), watch release health, and secure user data.
weeks.title: Performance, reliability and security

lessons.title: Startup performance
topics: Cold, warm and hot starts; time to initial and full display
Baseline Profiles and startup profiles
Measuring with Macrobenchmark
Deferring initialization and App Startup
lessons.exercise: Add a Baseline Profile to your app and measure cold start with Macrobenchmark before and after.

lessons.title: Jank, memory and ANRs
topics: Finding jank with Perfetto and system tracing
Memory leaks: common causes and LeakCanary
ANR causes: main-thread I/O, lock contention, slow broadcast receivers
Memory pressure and `onTrimMemory`
lessons.exercise: Record a Perfetto trace of a janky scroll, find the long frame's cause, and fix it.

lessons.title: Release health and observability
topics: Android vitals: crash rate, ANR rate and bad-behavior thresholds
Crash reporting and symbolication with R8 mapping files
Logging, analytics and feature flags in production
Running incident response for a bad release
lessons.exercise: Set crash-free and ANR targets for your app and write the runbook for a bad release.

lessons.title: Mobile security
topics: Android Keystore and encrypting data at rest
Token storage, network security config and certificate pinning trade-offs
Play Integrity API and tampering detection
OWASP Mobile Top 10 and MASVS
lessons.exercise: Audit your app against the OWASP Mobile Top 10 and fix the two worst findings.

milestones.title: Apply to five more roles and prepare questions to ask each company
DSA track: two timed mock coding rounds

weeks.deliverable: A performance report for your app: startup before and after Baseline Profiles, a fixed jank issue, a fixed leak, and a security checklist.
interview_checks: How do you measure and improve cold startup?
How do you find the cause of jank in a list?
What are the common causes of ANRs, and how do you find them in production?
Where do you store an auth token securely, and should you pin certificates?

weeks.goal: Pass the mobile system design round and the senior signals around it: AI features, leadership, code review and behavioral answers.
weeks.title: Mobile system design and the senior loop

lessons.title: Mobile system design: framework and a news feed
topics: A repeatable framework: requirements, API, data model, client architecture, deep dives
Designing a feed: pagination, caching, prefetching and image loading
Offline behavior and error handling in a design
Talking about trade-offs and adapting to interviewer feedback
lessons.exercise: Design a news feed in 45 minutes on a whiteboard and review it against the framework.

lessons.title: Real-time design: chat and messaging
topics: WebSockets vs push notifications vs polling
Message delivery states, ordering and retries
Local storage and sync for conversations
Battery and network cost of real-time features
lessons.exercise: Design a chat app with delivery receipts and offline sending, and defend the transport choice.

lessons.title: Library design and on-device AI
topics: Designing an image loader or file downloader: caching, cancellation, memory
Public API design for a library other teams use
On-device AI: Gemini Nano, ML Kit GenAI APIs and AppFunctions
Privacy, fallbacks and device support for AI features
lessons.exercise: Design an image loading library's API and caches, then sketch an on-device summarization feature with a fallback.

lessons.title: Leadership, code review and behavioral interviews
topics: The STAR method and senior signals: scope, ambiguity and influence
Mentoring, code review culture and driving technical decisions
Working effectively with AI coding assistants and agents
Running a live code-review round
lessons.exercise: Write and rehearse five STAR stories, and review a pull request aloud as you would in an interview.

milestones.title: Run a full mock loop: coding, mobile system design and behavioral, then fix the weakest answer

weeks.deliverable: Three rehearsed mobile system designs, five STAR stories and one full mock interview loop.
interview_checks: Design a news feed app with pagination, caching and image loading.
Design a chat app: when do you use WebSockets, push or polling?
Design an image loading library.
Tell me about a technical decision you drove that the team first disagreed with.
